newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-QUF sees recovery, but warns on div.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-QUF sees recovery, but warns on div.

text.p: Dairy foods group QUF Industries Ltd said on Tuesday it was expecting a recovery in profit in the current year, but may be forced to cut its dividend if this recovery did not occur.

"While your directors are expecting a recovery in profit in the current year which will justify maintaining the present dividend rate, a change will have to occur if it becomes clear that the necessary level of profit has not been achieved or is not in prospect," chairman Rod Wylie told the annual general meeting.
Wylie said the company was on track for the first quarter.
"We can see no indication at this time that some recovery is not in prospect," he told shareholders.

Wylie said it was still very early in the current year and emphasised that while there had been good first quarters in each of the last two financial years, results for both those years fell below early expectations.
"Obviously, a dividend rate which exceeds the reported profit cannot be justified or paid other than on a short term exception basis," he said.
Wylie confirmed that profit recoveries were expected in Victoria and the Nortern Territory.
However, he warned the new structure of the Australian Dairy Products industry had yet to become clear, following the entry of food giant Nestle and several other well known competitors.
"The scene is volatile and probably represents the greatest uncertainty for the current year," he said.
Another area under change was the national domestic UHT milk market.
Wylie said there had been a surge in low price sales of UHT milk domestically which was having a negative effect on market milk profitability for both producers and processors.
"Already UHT's market share of the domestic milk market has increased significantly at the expense of more traditional packaging, he said.
QUF shares were steady at A$2.66 at 1.30 p.m. (0230 GMT).
